report.summary: Index and typegraph diverge on module naming when .pyi stubs coexist or center-relative naming is used. Index's _PyNaming resolves canonical module per file (disambiguating .py/.pyi, stripping center prefix), while typegraph likely uses raw _py_dotted(rel), producing different module identifiers for the same file. This breaks cross-linking in downstream consumers (e.g., forest.py).
risks: Type nodes may reference a module name that does not exist in the index's module list (e.g., .pyi file name), causing dangling references.
When a .py and .pyi share a name, typegraph may create duplicate type node IDs if it does not disambiguate, or it may pick the wrong file.

Center-relative naming (e.g., stripping TCT_app/) in the index is not replicated in typegraph, so type node module ids will be repo-root dotted names, mismatching the package-relative names used in index records.
todos: Examine typegraph.py's module naming logic and compare with _PyNaming in index.py.
Test with fixture: repo containing a.py and a.pyi, and/or a file under a declared center.
Consider passing canonical module name map from index to typegraph, or making typegraph import naming from index.

handoff.suggestion: In index.py, after building _PyNaming, produce a dict mapping file path -> canonical module name (from _PyNaming._name[rel]), and pass it to typegraph so that type nodes use the same module identifier as the index. This avoids mismatch when .pyi disambiguation or center-relative naming is active.
